title: Flatten the tags of every post

blocks.text: The page contrasts `map()` and `flatMap()`: on a `List<List<String>>`, `map` keeps the nesting, while `flatMap(Collection::stream)` turns it into one `Stream<String>`. It also warns that null elements must be filtered out (`filter(Objects::nonNull)`) before a stream works on them.
Write `Tags.allTags(List<List<String>> posts)`. Each inner list is the tags of one post. Return every tag of every post as one list that is:

items: upper-cased with **`toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)`**, so the result does not depend on the machine's default locale (in Turkish, `"i"` upper-cases to `"İ"`),
free of duplicates, where two tags are duplicates when they are **equal after upper-casing** (the same text, even if each is its own `String` object),
without empty tags (`""`) and without `null` tags. A tag of spaces such as `" "` is not empty: keep it as it is.

cases.says: The tags of all posts come back as one sorted list of upper-case tags.
"Java" and "JAVA" become one tag, because duplicates are removed after upper-casing.
A tag that appears in several posts appears once, even when each post holds its own String object.
An empty tag "" is left out, while a tag of spaces is not empty and is kept as it is.
Tags are upper-cased the same way whatever the machine's default locale, even a Turkish one.
A null tag is left out instead of failing the whole call.

concepts: A stream pipeline declares what to do with filter, map, distinct and sorted instead of writing the iteration.
flatMap turns a stream of lists into one stream of their elements, where map would keep the nesting.
Null elements are filtered out with filter(Objects::nonNull) before a stream works on them.
